_comment: Agents known to be scheduled nowhere as of 2026-07-30, when check_orphan_agents() first ran. Accepted ONLY until the full board triages each one SCHEDULE/RETIRE/DELETE under proposal ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. This list may only ever SHRINK. Never add an entry to silence a new finding — a new orphan is a hard failure by design.
change_log: 2026-07-30 REMOVED dynamic_position_sizer.py, position_aging_agent.py — they no longer trip the check: neither writes an output that another module reads. (Both are still unscheduled; they are a lesser problem and stay in the ARCH triage.)

2026-07-30 ADDED ml_feature_drift_monitor.py, ml_longterm_label_checker.py — NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding. Two bugs in check_orphan_agents() were hiding them on the day this baseline was written: (1) test files were barred from being scheduler ROOTS but could still be pulled into the reachability set and relay from there, so the WIRED_AGENTS list added to test_pipeline_smoke.py made nine baselined orphans look scheduled; (2) the audit read only new_crontab.txt, a Mac-path TEMPLATE that had drifted 10 agents behind the VM's live crontab. Both are fixed; these two were always day-one orphans and belong in the same board triage.

2026-07-31 ADDED risk_limit_governor.py — NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding, same situation as the 2026-07-30 addition above. The reachability walk matched a module's name anywhere in another module's TEXT, so a mention inside a docstring or comment counted as a call; that prose reachability was hiding this agent. Fixed by walking code only (_code_only). Verified against ground truth before adding: the live VM crontab has 0 occurrences of risk_limit_governor across 67 job lines, and config.py:99 reads data/risk_limit_overrides.json in real code — a file this agent has never once produced, so config falls back to defaults and the asymmetric risk bands the sign-off ledger work added have never actually applied. Goes to the board with the other 11 under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents; my read is SCHEDULE.

2026-07-31 REMOVED risk_limit_governor.py, macro_regime_model.py, edgar_transcript_agent.py, institution_performance_tracker.py, ml_improvement_loop.py — SCHEDULE verdict under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. All five are now installed in the VM's live crontab (12:40 / 12:50 weekdays, 23:20 daily, Sun 07:40, Sat 06:30 UTC) and appear in data/vm_crontab_snapshot.txt, which is what the check measures against. Each was smoke-run on the VM at exit 0 BEFORE being scheduled — scheduling a producer means owning its output, and an agent that crashes on a cron is a louder failure than one that never runs. 12 known orphans → 7.

triage._comment: Verdicts for board proposal ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. Recorded 2026-07-31 with per-agent evidence. known_orphans is NOT shrunk here: an entry may only leave that list once the agent is actually in cron, and installing cron is the Chairman's call. Verdict != done.

apex_system_cit_agent.py.evidence: Runs clean on the VM (exit 0, 12 proposals raised). Writes chairman_action_required.json, read by 21 modules. Its own docstring says 'Runs daily at 1 PM UTC (cron: 0 13 * * *)' but the VM crontab has no such entry among 74 jobs — documented, never built. Its GCP-IP check was host-blind until 2026-07-31 (9d293a4); it is now metadata-gated and verified silent off-VM.

fi_cit_agent.py.evidence: Same consumed output contract (chairman queue, 21 readers). Exits 0.

ml_longterm_label_checker.py.evidence: Was blocked on a missing outcome_365d column; that is resolved and it exits 0. Writes ml_longterm_suggestions.json.

ml_validate_longterm.py.evidence: Exits 0. Writes longterm_validation_report.json, read by apex_improvement_board.py and ml_longterm_cit_agent.py.

ml_longterm_experiment_runner.py.evidence: Producer with no executable consumer. Its queue file has NEVER been produced. The upstream improvement agent's 9 suggestions carry no executable lever — this runner can only select a feature set, so bridging them would manufacture 9 results for 9 untested hypotheses. Guarded now by an UNRUNNABLE branch (c284e15). Schedule only after a suggestion format that names a lever this runner can actually pull.

ml_longterm_improvement_agent.py.evidence: Same bridge. Its output has no consumer that can act on it.

ml_feature_drift_monitor.py.blocker: recent window is calendar-based; its input is quarterly
ml_feature_drift_monitor.py.evidence: Verified on the VM: 'Recent window has only 0 rows (min 30). Skipping.' — recent=0, historical=24,576. Root cause is a design mismatch, not an outage: _fetch_windows() defines 'recent' as the last 60 days, but pipeline_snapshots is written on the 13F filing calendar — Feb/May/Aug/Nov, 2-3 distinct dates per quarter, unchanged for four years (last cluster 2026-05-15, next due mid-Aug). So for roughly two months in every three the recent window is empty BY CONSTRUCTION and this monitor can only skip. Scheduling it as-is buys a weekly no-op that reads like a clean run. Fix before scheduling: compare the latest filing cluster to the prior one, not a fixed 60/180-day window.
